Use this command family for dependent multi-entity changes that must be checked and applied as one reviewed unit.

### Availability
This Entry is a normative product contract. The command is implemented only when its canonical path appears in machine-readable `snl --help`; absence means planned and unavailable, never silently emulated through a different command.


### Command path
`batch` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The intended shell spelling is `snl batch`. Current availability is advertised by machine-readable `snl --help`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"batch","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Calling the namespace without a child is valid discovery, not a usage error.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"batch","data":{},"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains structured command discovery: child command paths, argument schemas, read/write classification, and one-line summaries.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"batch","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":{},"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Read-only. It must not acquire the writer lock or modify workspace bytes. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. Repeated calls against unchanged bytes return equivalent semantic results.

### Implemented create-only edition
The public allowlist is entry-kind/create, macro-kind/create, entry-package/create, macro-package/create, entry/create, macro/create, and relationship/create. References resolve against the complete candidate, so dependents may precede their prerequisites. Library, update, delete, rename, upsert and relationship/generate are not batch operations and reject the whole request. Package projections share one identity; nonempty authored entry_ids and embedded macros are rejected. Entry tags use the ordinary strict string-array contract and retain order and duplicates.

CLI check --input accepts a raw operations array; CLI apply --input accepts {operations,checkedDigest,expectedWorkspaceRevision}. Both accept a file or stdin, not a directory. Duplicate JSON properties, unknown command/argument keys and non-JSON JavaScript values reject, rather than being silently ignored. Discover schemas with snl batch --json or snl --help --json; MCP and DSH submit the same requests through snl_execute. Tokens are consistency guards, not signed credentials. See Skills/CLI Tools/Batch.md for the failure/recovery model.
